sections.text: Tasting the nectar of immortality, as the reward of sacrifice, they reach the Eternal. This world is not for those who refuse to sacrifice; much less the other world.
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।
In this way other sacrifices too may be undergone for the Spirits sake. Know thou that they all depend on action. Knowing this, thou shalt be free.
The sacrifice of wisdom is superior to any material sacrifice, O Arjuna. For all actions in their entirety culminate in wisdom.

Shri Purohit there is no comment on this sloka We had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga for renouncing actions in knowledge. So far we have seen that Bhagavan said that I am going to tell you a secret knowledge, having known which you will not have to know anything else. And this is nothing new.
I had been teaching this from the beginning of time how to end your actions. Thats the goal, to end my actions. But right now Im not finding any means to end these actions.
Bhagavan said that one who develops the knowledge that the self is not the doer can get out of this cycle of actions and reactions. The cycle continues: I act, the world reacts, that becomes actions for the world. When I react to that reaction, it becomes my actions, and the action-reaction cycle continues.
He said, once you get out of this notion that I am the doer, you will be out of this cycle of doing and reacting, suffering and enjoying. So in verse 14 he says namaam karmani lin panthi Namay karmafulesh prahaha ithimam yo vijayanathi karma bihin NASA badhyadhya. He is not bound by any actions.
One who knows me as Namam Karmani limpanti Karmas do not bind me, they do not attach to me. I dont get attached to the karma in Namay Karmafula. I do not have any desire for the Karma Phala that I is the self in me.
I think I have all these desires. Well, that I does not have any desires. My mind has desires, my intellect has desires, and also my body has desires.
It feels a little hot. My body tells me, lets make it comfortable. So all these things which I think I have karma falas pruha or the desire to enjoy is at either the body level, at the mind level or the intellect level.
At the self level there is no desire. The one who knows himself as the one has no attachment to action. Self never gets attached to any action.
Neither that self has any karma falas pruha. One who knows this as his own self in this manner he does not get bound by any actions. Another question is how do we get to that point? So in verse 23rd, the technique is Gatha Sangasya.
He has given up all attachments. He works in this world but does not get attached. He said the attachment to the world is like a post it notes.
As long as it is there, it is attached, you remove it. It does not leave any mark on their wall. Gatha Sangha says no attachment.
You can take it from here and put it here. And take it from here, put it here. It will get attached to whatever but not leave any mark. Gnana Vasthidha Saha.
So hes free, hes not attached. And his intellect is organized by the knowledge that the self is not having desire for any fruits of actions, neither it is taking part in any actions. Yajnaya Charathaha Karmaha.
And therefore he is constantly acting in the spirit of Yajna for the greater good. All the actions which are taking place are only taking place for the greater good, not just for my selfish desires. Karma sama Grim pravely. Thats how all the karmas will get destroyed for that person.
Hes not having any sense of identity with his actions. Then we have seen that this Yajna can be performed in various ways. But what should be the Yogi, the one who has mastered this art of performing actions in Yajna, his attitude.
There are two ways he said. The first one he says is Devam Evapare, Yajnam Yogi, Nahapariupa Sataya. Some yogis will perform all their actions working in this world, experiencing this world as the world is offering its objects for the perception of his senses.
Worlds offering to the senses. Its not him going to the world, world coming to him. Thats how he never gets attached to him.
Because he is not really going out to the world. World is coming to him for his perception. So all the perception comes and goes, but he never gets attached to any one of them.
Thats the one way other. Brahma Agnavare Yagnam Yagne Eva Upa Jihuvati. Others will sacrifice the self by the self.
And the next verse is Brahmarpanam Brahmavi. Everything that is happening is happening by the self alone. So now that when Im working in this world, Im offering myself which I consider to be myself right now is my sense of perception.
Sense organs of actions in the service of the self, the greater self. So now everything which Im doing is offering to the self by myself. The limited self offering its own self for the service of the self.
In this attitude, when he works in this world, hes also not getting attached to any actions because he obviously is not really performing any actions for himself. So both are the various ways the Yogi sees this world. Either this way where the world is offering to himself, or he is offering himself to the greater self.
Both are the techniques with which he can continue working in this world, but not getting attached to the actions. And then we have seen that the agnas can be performed in 12 different ways. The fire you have to kindle for this yajna is not the physical fire, but the fire of your self restraint.
So Samyama Agni, hes going to start with kindling first his fire of restraint. That restraint first can be at this sense level, sensual perceptions he limits to a point where he does not get attached to them. So restraining the senses is the first method we use it.
The second method is the mental restraining the perception. So whatever the perception comes, he obviously restrain its impression, does not let that perception leave any impression on his mind. So its a mental level.
And the next level of yajnas we have seen is the intellectual level, Swadhyaya Yajna. I constantly reflect on what is the truth about myself. Constantly asking question, who is it that tells me that I am doing this? So thats swadhya yajna at the intellectual level, which is we call gnana yajna.
Then Bhagavan also enumerated that there are other yajnas as well. But all of them we have seen is performing yajnas in the mental level. By kindling the fire of restraint, restraining of the senses, restraining of the mind, or restraining the intellect into the inquiry of what is the self.
We have seen there are other methods available. There is not really one method fits all we know because human beings are made in various different permutations and combinations. Sattva, rajas and Tamas, whichever is most conducive for me, I should be practicing.
But the goal is to perform actions in Yajna spirit. Thats basically the goal. Evam, Bahvida, Yajna, Vitatha, Brahmana, mukhe.
Thus there are many yajnas lying at the mouth of Brahman. These are not the only yajnas that can be practiced. But theres a limitation for the poet -- he cannot enumerate a list of thousands of Yajnas.
There are many methods available to you. Vitatha Brahmanamukha -- they are scattered at the mouth of Brahman, at the gate leading to Brahman, at the threshold of perception of the Brahman. There are many paths which are leading towards that that will open the door for you.
So any of that, whatever path I take, as long as I have taken the correct path towards my goal, that goal will be available to me. Karma Janaan Vidhi Taan, Sarvaan Evam Gnatva Vimoksha Se. But know that all those paths are born out of actions. In other words, you cannot sit back and relax and say things will be done and someday I will have a realization.
It requires your self-effort. No matter which path you take, there is no easy shortcut. All of them require you to put your own self-effort to get there. Karma Jan Viddhi -- there is not a single path where you just stay relaxed and it comes to you.
Actions are very much essential in each part. Actions are the binding force right now and Im trying to get out of it. Actions are the only means available to me to get to Brahman.
As long as I put my self efforts on a right path. Bhagavan says Vimoksha Se you will achieve the moksha. As long as I take the right route to go to New York.
Whether I take 95 north through the New Jersey Turnpike or go via Route 95 through Philadelphia -- as long as I know that this path is leading towards my goal. Just sitting down here thinking about it, I will never go to New York. But putting my efforts into it -- Tan Sarvan Evam Ganatwa Vimoksha Sey -- theyre all going to take you to the same goal as long as you put your self-effort in a diligent and honest manner.
So the next verse says Sreyan Dravyam Yagnath Gnana Yajnaha Parantabah Sarva Karma Ahilam Partha Gnane Parisamarpiate -- which path should I take? He said the Gnana Yajna is clearly better than the Dravya Yajna. This is not an indication that this all the various paths which are described as one is better than other. All paths are gonna lead you.
As long as you put your self efforts in a clear understanding what my goal is will get you there. However, the culture in the environment may mislead me. Me just writing a check to the Hindu Center -- I think that I have earned some punyas.
Bhagavan says that Dravya Yajna will get you very little, because the whole intention behind writing the check makes that check what it is worth to you, not to the Hindu Center. The Hindu Center gets the same value. I write a check for $101 -- the $101 they can cash.
But whether that gives me value is all about my intentions. What efforts did I put in, with what intentions, with what understanding -- that will determine my reward. Therefore he says Sreyan Dravyam Yagnath Gnana Yajnah Paramta.
Whatever your perception of that offering, as long as the knowledge does not take place, that offering does not get you much. Therefore knowledge is superior to the physical act of performing Yajna. I may be exercising, but not with a clear understanding of what Im trying to get out of it.
Then obviously it wont have the same result as exercising with a clear goal. Disciplined actions with a clear plan, clear knowledge of what this action should yield -- that will get you much greater results. And you go to American Fitness.
Do you have a trainer? I dont have a trainer. Why do I need a trainer? That trainer will give you this gnana. Which exercise will be better for you? I may be putting lot of efforts but in a wrong direction.
Yesterday we were at somebodys house and somebody took out of the list of what food does not goes with what. In the end we said if you follow this, we will not be able to eat anything. He said parotta should not be eaten with dahi yogurt.
So Punjabis are all gone! See, even that knowledge, if it is put in the right context, may have some value. Obviously the whole of our Ayurveda is about parhej. You have to regulate your diet, and then you dont need other medication.
But just doing upavas without thinking may actually make me sick.

Verse 31 declares that those who partake of the nectar remaining from yajna attain the eternal Brahman, while those who perform no yajna find no happiness even in this world, let alone the next. Verse 32 reveals that many types of yajna are spread before Brahmans gate, and all are born of action (karmajan). Knowing this, one becomes liberated. Verse 33 makes a crucial distinction: Shreyan dravyamayad yajnat jnana-yajnah - the sacrifice of knowledge is superior to material sacrifice, for all actions in their entirety culminate in knowledge (sarvam karmakhilam partha jnane parisamapyate).
This teaching clarifies that while many paths exist, knowledge (jnana) is the ultimate goal toward which all other practices lead. Writing a charity check has value, but the intention and understanding behind it determines its true worth. The same external action performed with different levels of awareness produces vastly different results. Like having a trainer at the gym who guides your efforts optimally, knowledge directs and elevates all other practices. Without understanding why you are doing something, even sincere effort may be misdirected.
For daily practice, evaluate not just what you do but the knowledge underlying it. Before any spiritual practice - whether charity, discipline, or study - ask: What am I trying to achieve? How does this lead toward self-knowledge? Just as the teaching says all paths are karma-jan (born of action), your own efforts are indispensable. There is no shortcut where things happen without your participation. Today, choose one practice and examine the knowledge component: What do you understand about why this works? What are you still confused about? Evam jnatva vimokshyase - knowing thus, you shall be liberated. Make your practice conscious, not mechanical.
